card.title: TIGERCAT
card.text: At the end of your turn, add a SBD 3 DAUNTLESS to your support line.
card.flavorText: The Grumman F7F Tigercat was a twin-engine heavy fighter designed for the US Navy. Developed in response to a 1941 demand for a fast, long-range aircraft with heavy armament, it first flew in 1943. The Tigercat was equipped with four 20 mm cannons and four 12.7 mm machine guns, along with underwing racks for bombs, rockets or torpedoes. It was one of the fastest piston-engine fighters of the war, significantly outpacing the F6F Hellcat at low altitude. Despite its performance, the Tigercat faced challenges. Its large size and heavy weight made it difficult to operate from standard aircraft carriers. Early models struggled with directional control on one engine and had problems with carrier landings. Only the final variant, the F7F-4N, was certified for carrier use, and very few were produced. The Tigercat arrived too late to see combat in WWII. Marine reconnaissance units used it for mapping invasion beaches in the Pacific in mid-1945. It later saw limited action during the Korean War, primarily in night fighter and ground attack roles. The aircraft remained in service with the Marine Corps until the early 1950s.
